summary: Troyes uses dice as workers, rolled each round and distributed among three color-coded 'action pools' representing the city's religious, military, and civil life, which players then spend from a shared communal supply to fuel their hand of cards. It's a clever hybrid of worker-placement and hand management with a strong economic push-your-luck feel, since dice can be stolen or bribed away from you.
praised: inventive dice-as-workers mechanism with real tactical depth
good economic tension from paying opponents to use their dice
compact playtime for the strategic weight
criticised: dice luck can swing outcomes despite mitigation options
hidden victory-point cards make it hard to gauge the score during play
fiddly bookkeeping with multiple resource types
art and theme feel a bit flat for some players

interaction.kind: shared dice pool and paid worker borrowing
interaction.detail: The dice pool generated each round is shared, and players can pay opponents to use their dice or lose their own to misfortune events, so there's constant low-level negotiation over a common resource even though each player's card hand and building track stay private.

sources: character card bonus VP (one per character card in play, each with its own criteria)
scoring.how_you_win: Across a preset number of rounds (set by how many red event cards are seeded in, 4-6 depending on player count) you place die-workers to build the cathedral, contest event cards, staff activity spaces, and satisfy character-card conditions; whoever has summed the most victory points across all these sources when the last event card resolves wins.
